verses.zh: （大卫的诗。）耶和华啊，我要求告你！我的磐石啊，不要向我缄默！倘若你向我闭口，我就如将死的人一样。
verses.en: By David.To you, O Lord, I cry out!My Protector,[NOTE:1] do not ignore me.[NOTE:2] If you do not respond to me,[NOTE:3] I will join[NOTE:4] those who are descending into the grave.[NOTE:5]
notes: Psalm 28. The author looks to the Lord for vindication, asks that the wicked be repaid in full for their evil deeds, and affirms his confidence that the Lord will protect his own.
Heb “my rocky summit.” The Lord is compared to a rocky summit where one can find protection from enemies. See Ps 18:2.
Heb “do not be deaf from me.”
Heb “lest [if] you are silent from me.”
Heb “I will be equal with.”

verses.zh: 我呼求你，向你至圣所举手的时候，求你垂听我恳求的声音！
verses.en: Hear my plea for mercy when I cry out to you for help,when I lift my hands[NOTE:1] toward your holy temple.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the pit.” The noun בּוֹר (bor, “pit, cistern”) is sometimes used of the grave and/or the realm of the dead.
I lift my hands. Lifting one’s hands toward God was a gesture of prayer.

verses.zh: 不要把我和恶人并作孽的一同除掉；他们与邻舍说和平话，心里却是奸恶。
verses.en: Do not drag me away with evil men,with those who behave wickedly,[NOTE:1] who talk so friendly to their neighbors,[NOTE:2] while they plan to harm them.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew term דְּבִיר (devir, “temple”) actually refers to the most holy place within the sanctuary.
Heb “workers of wickedness.”
Heb “speakers of peace with their neighbors.”

verses.zh: 愿你按着他们所做的，并他们所行的恶事待他们。愿你照着他们手所做的待他们，将他们所应得的报应加给他们。
verses.en: Pay them back for their evil deeds.Pay them back for what they do.Punish them.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and evil [is] in their heart[s].”

verses.zh: 他们既然不留心耶和华所行的和他手所做的，他就必毁坏他们，不建立他们。
verses.en: For they do not understand the Lord’s actions,or the way he carries out justice.[NOTE:1] The Lord[NOTE:2] will permanently demolish them.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Give to them according to their work, and according to the evil of their deeds. According to the work of their hands give to them. Return their due to them.” The highly repetitive style reflects the psalmist’s agitated emotional state and draws attention to his yearning for justice.

Heb “or the work of his hands.” In this context “the Lord’s actions” and “the work of his hands” probably refer to the way he carries out justice by vindicating the godly and punishing the wicked. (Note the final line of the verse, which refers to divine judgment. See also Ps 92:4-7.) Evil men do not “understand” God’s just ways; they fail to realize he will protect the innocent. Consequently they seek to harm the godly, as if they believe they will never be held accountable for their actions.
Heb “he”; the referent (the Lord, who is referred to in the two immediately preceding lines) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 耶和华是应当称颂的，因为他听了我恳求的声音。
verses.en: The Lord deserves praise,[NOTE:1] for he has heard my plea for mercy.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “will tear them down and not rebuild them.” The ungodly are compared to a structure that is permanently demolished.
Heb “blessed [be] the Lord.”

verses.zh: 耶和华是我的力量，是我的盾牌；我心里倚靠他就得帮助。所以我心中欢乐，我必用诗歌颂赞他。
verses.en: The Lord strengthens and protects me;[NOTE:1] I trust in him with all my heart.[NOTE:2] I am rescued[NOTE:3] and my heart is full of joy;[NOTE:4] I will sing to him in gratitude.[NOTE:5]
notes: He has heard my plea for mercy. The psalmist’s mood abruptly changes at this point because the Lord responded positively to his petition and assured him that he would deliver him.
Heb “The Lord [is] my strength and my shield.”
Heb “in him my heart trusts.”
Or “I am helped.”
Heb “and my heart exults.”

verses.zh: 耶和华是他百姓的力量，又是他受膏者得救的保障。
verses.en: The Lord strengthens his people;[NOTE:1] he protects and delivers his chosen king.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and from my song I will thank him.” As pointed in the Hebrew text, מִשִּׁירִי (mishiri) appears to be “from my song,” but the preposition “from” never occurs elsewhere with the verb “to thank” (Hiphil of יָדָה, yadah). Perhaps משׁיר is a noun form meaning “song.” If so, it can be taken as an adverbial accusative, “and [with] my song I will thank him.” See P. C. Craigie, Psalms 1-50 (WBC), 236.

Heb “the Lord [is] strength to them” (or perhaps, “to him”). The form לָמוֹ (lamo, “to them/him”) probably needs to be emended to לְעַמּוֹ (leʿammo, “to his people”; see P. C. Craigie, Psalms 1-50 [WBC], 236), perhaps due to quiescence of the letter ʿayin (ע; see P. McCarter, Textual Criticism [GBS], 55). Note the reference to the Lord’s “people” in the next verse. Also, a few Hebrew mss, the LXX, and Syriac support לְעַמּוֹ (leʿammo, “to his people”).

verses.zh: 求你拯救你的百姓，赐福给你的产业，牧养他们，扶持他们，直到永远。
verses.en: Deliver your people.Empower[NOTE:1] the nation that belongs to you.[NOTE:2] Care for them like a shepherd and carry them in your arms[NOTE:3] at all times![NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “he [is] a refuge of help for his anointed one.” The noun מָשִׁיחַ (mashiakh, “anointed one”) refers to the Davidic king, who perhaps speaks as representative of the nation in this psalm. See Pss 2:2; 18:50; 20:6; 84:9; 89:38, 51; 132:10, 17.
Or “bless.”
Heb “your inheritance.” The parallelism (note “your people”) indicates that Israel is in view.
The shepherd metaphor is sometimes associated with royal responsibility. See 2 Sam 5:2; 7:7; Mic 5:2-4).tn Heb “shepherd them and lift them up.”
